utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: In the absence of Judge Van Den Wyngaert, Judge David and I sit pursuant it to the provisions of Rule 15 bis. Just a few matters before we begin. On the 1st of April, the Prosecution filed a motion for reconsideration of or in the alternative certification to appeal the Chamber's decision of 25th March, 2009, concerning rebuttal witnesses. The Chamber considers that expedited responses are necessary and orders that any responses are to be filed by noon, Monday the 6th of April. The Chamber has reviewed the submission -- private session, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: On the 20th of March, the Prosecution made an oral request that the Chamber authorise the Registrar to provide the Prosecution with photographs of Prosecution witnesses, the purpose being to allow it to prepare a confidential exhibit for its cross-examination of Milan Lukic. Milan Lukic has indicated that he will not testify in his own Defence; and therefore, the Chamber dismisses that request as moot. On the 18th of March, the Prosecution made an oral application requesting the Chamber to amend schedule A of the indictment by removing the names of alleged victims, Latifa Kurspahic, Lejla Kurspahic, and Mejva Kurspahic. The Defence of Milan Lukic opposed the Prosecution's application. The Chamber will defer its decision on the Prosecution's application until after the close of evidence in this case. I want to inform the parties that in the interest of time, the Chamber has asked the VWS to assist in bringing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I was just checking if this had to be in private session. I wanted to say that in the interest of time, the Chamber has asked the VWS to assist in bringing VG-61 to testify as a Defence witness. Let the witness be brought in.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, while the witness is being brought in,

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alarid. So we have to redact, then, the discussion, the entire discussion. That's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let the witness make the declaration. Please make the declaration. Please read the declaration. The witness is apparently not hearing me.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please sit. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Good day, sir. As you know, I'm Dan Ivetic and I'm one of the attorneys for Milan Lukic here today, and I have some questions to discuss with you. I'd like to remind you at the outset that we ought to speak at a measured pace to allow the transcript and the translators to keep up with us. Is that fair, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And also, our responses will need to be verbal so that the transcript picks them up. Now, to start with, can we please have your full name stated and spelled for the record.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: My name is Zoran Uscumlic. Zoran Uscumlic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And before I get too far into this, Your Honours, one document that we had intended to utilise with this witness somehow became omitted from our list that we submitted the other day to the Prosecution before -- we're not going to be using that document at the beginning of the examination, but I'd like to let them know that 2D60 is also a document that we will have the witness comment upon to give them time to track that down and review it. It's another list from the police station, horizontally.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, Mr. Uscumlic, could you tell us, sir, first of all, are you here today in your personal capacity, or are you here in an official capacity?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I was summoned. I don't know in what capacity, but I was summoned through the Ministry of the Interior. I don't know who summoned me.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. If you could confirm for us that your attendance today is pursuant to a subpoena issued by this Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And first of all, sir, so we can get it out of the way, do you in fact know Milan Lukic; that is to say, are you friends or acquaintances with Milan Lukic, and are you related to Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I'm not related to Milan Lukic. We never met formally, but we do know each other. We just know each other by sight.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you tell us, first of all, what is your official capacity, that is to say, what is the current position that you hold in your employment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I am the commander of the Visegrad police station, which is part of the East Sarajevo Public Security Centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir, and again, I'm pausing to allow the translation into English and the transcript to catch up with us. Could you summarise for us briefly the job duties and authorities that you hold -- and authority that you hold as the commander of the police station in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: As the police station commander, I'm the number one person in the police station; and our authorities, meaning the authority of the police station, is to control crimes, public law and order, and all activities in our jurisdiction that are covered by our area of responsibility as well as any kind of citizen events.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And with respect to -- you said that you were the number one person in the police station. With respect to the current makeup and structure of the police station, what has become of the position that used to be known as chief of the police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, the chief of police station post was abolished some three or four years ago so that the police station commander, a uniformed commander is the number one official of the police station. The post of chief was considered a political function, and that is why it was abolished.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, you indicated that you are currently the commander of the Visegrad police station. How long have you held this position within the Visegrad police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I was appointed to that post on the 15th of July, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now before that, could you tell us how long it is that you have served as a professional policeman in the MUP, the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: As a police officer, from 1987, the first post I had was in the public security centre in Gorazde. Then I worked at the public security station in Gorazde. Then when the MUP broke apart, I became the commander of the Gorazde police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, 1987 to 2006 is a long time. Could you tell us what position you held immediately prior to becoming the commander of the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Before that, I was commander of the police station Novo Gorazde in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the sake of your background, if you could just merely explain to us from where -- where is it you were born and when were you born?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I was born on the 5th of May, 1962, in Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And could you detail for us briefly the circumstances around your coming to be appointed to your current position as the commander of the police station in Visegrad, whom it is you replaced, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, I was appointed to that position of the commander of the police station in Visegrad on the decision of the chief of the Public Security Centre, East Sarajevo, Mr. Zoran Mandic. That was on the 15th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at the time that you became the police commander in Visegrad by this -- I guess it was a decision or decree, who was the commander you were replacing, and was that person present, or had they left that position at some point in time prior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: When I came to the workplace of commander, the prior commander of the police station was no longer there. There was only his deputy because the commander had been assigned to new duties a year before in the MUP of Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now, if you could tell us a little bit about the structure of the MUP, specifically the organ of the MUP that you belonged to. What is the territorial jurisdiction that your police station covers?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, just to interrupt just for a foundational purpose. If we could at least specify the dates because the witness is indicating there is a different structure to the MUP at different times.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, with respect to your current position and the current police station that you are the head of, could you tell us what is the territorial jurisdiction of that police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The area of Visegrad municipality, the entire Visegrad municipality of 485 square metres -- sorry, kilometres.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are the dates, Mr. Ivetic? What are the dates that this covers, to deal with Mr. Weber's point.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe -- I thought I specified that, Your Honour, but it looks like -- looking at the transcript that I had not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: When you became commander of the police station in 2006, and from that date forward, I presume you've been in that position, has the territorial jurisdiction that you've just described remained the same?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Are you asking me when? Yes, on the 15th of July, 2006.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In terms of the time-period of 1992, that is to say during the hostilities that erupted on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina within the SFRY, do you have knowledge of the makeup and structure of the police, the Ministry of Interior at that point in time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina was structured in such a way that there were five Security Services Centres. Each Security Services Centre had a department of public and a department of state security; and in each Security Services Centre, there existed public security stations. That was the composition. We belonged to the Security Services Centre of Gorazde, which had in its composition six public security stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, with respect to the territorial jurisdiction that your police station now covers, do you have knowledge of what entity within the MUP covered that same jurisdiction in 1992 during the course of the -- of the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That territory was covered by the public security station of Visegrad within the framework of the Security Services Centre of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have any other organs apart from your own police station inherited the duties, responsibilities, and property of that security service -- public security station of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I did not really understand this question. I don't know which property you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Let's take a step back, first of all. Maybe we do need to talk about the types of assets. Now, first of all, within the police station, what types of identity documents or personal documents are kept in the police station and/or issued by the police station in the course of your ordinary practice?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, sorry to interrupt, but it's going to be important I believe that this witness's testimony dates -- whether he is testifying as current knowledge or the manner in which the MUP operated back in 1992. So I just please ask during the course of the testimony if the witness could specify whether or not they were referring to their current position and how records are currently kept or if he is specifying as to how records were kept in 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: That should not be difficult.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I've been very conscious to use the terminology from this time-period, which is police station. The prior time period was public security station, so I've been very careful to try to keep the witness on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, sir, in answering the question if you could also tell us whether in fact the duties and obligations of the police in respect to personal documents, if they have changed any from before the war to after the war in Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Documents were issued exactly in the same way after the war until the CIBC [as interpreted] project until now when documents are issued completely differently.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you say documents were issued in exactly the same way, where were the records of these documents stored or kept?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Documents were issued to private persons and the files and other documentation were kept in the archives.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect -- I apologise. We have to slow down a little bit for the translation, I'm told. We have -- with respect to these documents that were issued to private persons, and you say the files and other documentation were kept in the archives. With respect to those personal documents, where are those archives located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: If we are talking about IDs and other similar documents, there were filing rooms, offices, manned by personnel, clerks in charge of IDs, vehicle registration papers, and such.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to those files and those archives, sir, do those continue to exist to this day within your police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: In our police station, there exists files for all the IDs that have been issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Just a few more questions to finish up on the hierarchy to we can understand how your entity functions in its official capacity. Within the hierarchy of the MUP, what body or organ does the Visegrad police station fall under and report to directly?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The police station of Visegrad was an internal organisational unit of the Ministry of the Interior. It is directly subordinated to the Security Services Centre as an organisational unit of the MUP. In this case, it's the Security Services Centre of Sarajevo, which itself is subordinated to the Security Services Centre in Banja Luka, the head office.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with regard to the MUP of Republika Srpska, including Visegrad and yourself, am I correct that personnel must meet certain criteria and obtain certification, and could you detail for us what kind of certification is required?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, every authorised officer must go through vetting and certification. We, the older generation, were certified by the ITF [as interpreted], and even nowadays, current officer candidates have to go through the certification process at the MUP, again, regulated by the IPTF.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, in your response you've mentioned twice the IPTF. For those of us unfamiliar with this acronym, could you explain for us, what is the IPTF?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's the International Police Task Force that had been present in our territory until the arrival of the European police. Their role was -- is to supervise, to monitor, and to give suggestions for improvement to all police stations.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And have you had the occasion to cooperate with the international police forces and/or the European police that have been overseers on the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina during the time-period following the conclusion of the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: All police stations were duty-bound to cooperate with them. Later on, each police station even had an office housing representatives of the IPTF who oversaw the daily work of managers and all the personnel of the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in the course of your duties as commander of the police station in Visegrad, have you had occasion to respond to requests for assistance or requests for documentation from organs or parties before this International Tribunal for the Former Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, those requests are very frequent, and with each of them we provided an answer based on our documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, you've already told us about the personal documentation that is stored at the police station as to residence or citizens. Can I ask you to clarify for us what is the JMBG number, JMBG, and its significance to citizens of the state?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: JMBG is the unique citizens identification number which every citizen of our state is issued with at birth, and that number follows him throughout his life. There can be no duplicates of JMBG.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. You've anticipated my second question as to whether there can be duplications. Now, with respect to the --

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Absolutely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, with respect to the requests from parties -- with respect to the parties that have sent requests for assistance to your offices, how do those requests for assistance arrive to your facility to be processed? Is there a procedure for that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: For the most part, RFAs would be forwarded by the Security Services Centre of Sarajevo through the MUP towards us, and we in turn sent our replies via the MUP, unless the request for assistance was addressed directly to us.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And did you have occasion, sir, to receive a request for assistance from myself and the Defence of Milan Lukic asking you to search the records of the MUP and provide certain documentation?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did receive the request to check certain persons on the two lists that you've provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the record, the two lists in question are annexes A and B of the indictment. If we can call up 1D22-0800.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I would just ask this these lists not be broadcast, prior to the transmission, just because of some of the names on them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, that will be done.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. As a matter of fact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. The court deputy will see to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just to be efficient. I don't know if counsel plans on referring to specific names. If there's going to be specific names referred to, the Prosecution would submit, then we can just go into private session. If counsel is just going to be referring to it generally for the purposes of foundation, we have no problem staying in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Which is it, Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Waiting for the translation, Your Honour. We are not going to be referring to names. We're seeking to admit this document. It has been part of our bar table submission. I'm just laying the foundation for the generation of this document, how it was produced, based upon what review, and whether the witness has knowledge that might assist the Trial Chamber in considering this document and the information contained therein. I will be seeking to either admit the document after that, but then I would already ask that this particular document be done under seal because I note that it's not the redacted form that I would need because there's one name that needs to be redacted, and I will, of course, make sure a redacted copy is -- a public copy is provided at some point in time, hopefully later today, with respect to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we have a document now up on the screen. We have both the English translation and the original Serb version on the right-hand side. Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I recognise it. It's the document we sent to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to this document, sir, if could you please just highlight for us what you and/or those subordinate to you within the police station did upon receipt of our request in order to generate this document and the information that is contained within this document; and again, without referring to specific names of persons who might be mentioned in the document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, you submitted to us a request containing a certain number of names, around 70 names on the first list and around 10 on the second list, and we were asked to run checks through the old manual database to see if any of these names are on the old database. There was no unique citizens number or the date of birth or any information on that list, just name, surname, and approximate age. And based on that, I instructed our officer in charge of IDs to look up the older database and take out the files if she finds any, and she singled out certain files based on which I made a list, and that list we are now seeing on the monitor. We submitted, in other words, a list of persons with those names and surnames. We are not sure they are exactly the same persons that are meant on your list, but they have the names and surnames that correspond.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the list that I submitted to you for processing in this manner, were there persons on that list for whom you could not find the correlating original identification records within the archives of the police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's why we used these sequential numbers from your list. We skipped the numbers we did not find matches for. If we did not find any matches, we did not provide any information.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And with the assistance of the court officials, I'd like to move to the second page of this document in -- well, in both languages, but the B/C/S is the most instructive.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And sir, as you can see now, there is a -- if you could focus on the signature. I'm sorry. The signature and the seal that is visible here, sir, are those familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's my signature and the stamp of the police station of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And looking at this document, can you vouch for this document being the document that your police station generated in response to my request for assistance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can confirm that. It's an original document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would move to admit this document -- this particular version under seal as the next available 1D Exhibit number with, of course, a public redacted version to be provided, again, hopefully some time today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just wanted to confirm, is counsel moving in 1D22-0802 through 0803 -- I'm sorry, 0804, and then the corresponding B/C/S version, which is -- the original, I believe, is 1D22-0800 through 0801?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That is correct. That's how they are linked in e-court, and that's how they're appearing on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. As long as it's just those documents, no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 1D220 under seal, and the public redacted version will become Exhibit 1D221.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Did you have occasion, sir, to also to send the information that you obtained back up the chain of command within the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Simultaneously with your request, a request came from the MUP, that is from the centre for public security, and it was an identical request to yours, so I submitted the same response to the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And now, if you could just focus for a second back on the records that are your police station, these cards or archives; I think in Serbian you said the word "kartons," "kartona." With respect to these items, you indicated I believe that they were later supplemented by the CIPC system. Could you tell us a little bit about the CIPC system? The C-I-P-C.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, that's an integrated system for the whole territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina that was launched in 2003. It's a unified database for all citizens of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Data is collected individually in all police stations, and it is accessible to all police stations in the territory of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And do you know or have you seen any additional information or response generated by the higher organs in the MUP or within the government of Bosnia-Herzegovina relating to the list that you forwarded in response to my request for assistance?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No. I just responded to their letter with that document I drafted, and there was no reaction.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'd like to ask you, when you became commander of the police station in Visegrad, did you inherit any documents from the previous holders of your office, that is to say, any other archives in addition to the personal identity archives that you've already described that were held in a separate office?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No. Unfortunately, those archives were missing when I took over. For some reason, it's missing from the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What about any unofficial documents that -- were there any unofficial documents that you discovered in the office when you moved in as the commander of the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: In the safe which was in the office of the police station, I found some documents from that period, the wartime period, and I actually found only one list of the reserve and active police members that was drafted in 1992. I found an unsigned list from 1992 from June, the list of active and reserve members of the police force of the Visegrad public security station. I also found a list from 2002, August 2002 on, and these are order lists that exist still.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can have document -- actually, I think it's Exhibit 2D60 on the screen. I believe this is the one that we've seen in this trial previously.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And in one moment, sir, on the screen, we'll get a document. Do you recognise this document that is now appearing on the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That is the list of the conscripts that participated in the war who were -- had their wartime assignment in the public security station in Visegrad for that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we see a stamp in the upper right-hand corner of this document. Are you familiar with that stamp, and if so, what stamp is it, and what time-period was it utilised during?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The stamp certifies the list which I signed. I was requested to provide the list from the MUP, and they asked me to certify each page that I copied with the stamp of the Visegrad police station, so this is the police station of Visegrad stamp and my signature on every page.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, you've not -- strike that. You indicated, am I correct, that this is one of the documents that you found in the safe in the commander's office when you assumed that position in 2006?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you have any personal knowledge as to when this document was created and for what purposes it was created?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, at the end of the list there is the signature of the then public security station chief, Dragan Nisic, who signed the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you have any way of knowing whether this document was prepared before or after the disappearance of the remaining archives of the police station of Visegrad that you testified to earlier?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I can assume that the document was created at that time because you can see there's a large number of conscripts from the reserve and active police forces, and mostly people were on that list because they wanted to claim some sort of benefits or implement some sort of rights.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please slow down a little.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, you are being asked by the interpreter to speak more slowly.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. Now, with respect to this list that the -- if I'm understanding you correctly, it appears to have been generated by persons asking for their name to be put on the list. Is that an accurate -- am I understanding you correctly?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Objection, calls for speculation as to what those other people intended.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, do you know why those persons asked for their names to be put on list?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think that anyone asked to be put on the list, individual people to be put on the list, but I think that the members of the police or the chief of the public security station at the time in Visegrad in order to make his work easier made this list so that he could have a list in one place of all the military conscripts who were in the war -- who were members of the public security station in Visegrad during the war. I don't think that the list was drafted at the request of individuals, but it was a decision of the public security station chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Continue, Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about some individuals. First of all, are you familiar with a gentleman who was by the name of Dragan Tomic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him. I knew the late Dragan Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the time-period of the war during 1992, are you familiar with what position Dragan Tomic held?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Dragan Tomic at the beginning of the war was the commander of the Visegrad police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And if we can turn to the fourth page of the list in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, this list is prepared somewhat alphabetically, and I'd ask you to look at pages 4 and 5 under this list, under the Ts, and tell me whether in fact the particular Dragan Tomic that you know as being the commander of the Visegrad police station during the war, if he is listed on this document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't see his name on the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And yet you are certain that he was, indeed, an official member of the police station of Visegrad in 1992, the time-period that this list purports to cover?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I'm sure that he was the commander of the police station. I don't know why he is not on the list. Perhaps it's because he is no longer alive. In any case, the Tomic who is on the list is not him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the sake of completeness, if we could have page 5, as well, because I believe the Ts also go on to page 5, as well, and just show that to the witness so he has a full opportunity to review all the Ts because I believe there is another Tomic at 148.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Is that individual listed as number 148 the Dragan Tomic that you know to have been the commander of the police station in Visegrad in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, no, definitely not.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. I'm done with that document. I'd like to now turn to some other documents that the Prosecution has provided us relative to the Visegrad police station; and thus, I'd like to call up P209 first, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, we see a document that is now coming up on the screen. This is the Prosecution's Exhibit 209 in this case. Is this a document that you have seen in the course of your -- in the course of your duties as commander of the police station of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't have this document at the police station. I can comment on it, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. First of all, sir, can you tell us whether in fact this document could have come from your police station; that is to say, are you involved in every request for assistance and documentation that is sent officially from the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I assume that this is a document from the public security centre because this is a salary list. It was probably sent from the police station, but there isn't a copy of this document at the police station right now, so probably this is from the public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And would that be the -- which -- where is that public security centre located?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The public security centre in East Sarajevo, but in view of the date, 1992, this was then under the jurisdiction of the Trebinje public security centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could turn to the last page and focus on the signature and the stamp on the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like you to take a look at this section where this document was signed and stamped. One moment. One moment, please. With respect to -- with respect to, first of all, the stamp, do you recognise this stamp as one that was authorised for use within the MUP or ever used in the MUP officially?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, no. The stamp with these marks, at least as far as I know, was never used. We never used any kind of stamp with the markings such as the ones in the centre of this stamp.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think that document we are done with. P213, if we can have that up on the screen, and if we could again go to the last page of that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I don't seem to have a print-out of that one, but I'd like to see if that seal is the same as the one ...

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's the same stamp as in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the -- you indicated, I believe -- you paid particular attention to the markings in the centre of the stamp. For the sake of clarity, which particular markings are you making reference to as having not been part of the official stamps that were in use by the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The cross with the four Ss is what I mean, but it's very easy to check what sort of a stamp was used. If you send it for analysis to the MUP of the Republic of Serbia, that would be the most competent body that could provide the best answer for this kind of thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And am I to take it from your answer, then, that all official stamps or seals in use of the MUP are registered in the central MUP headquarters?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Again, if we could have some foundation as to when. Currently? Back in 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: In the course of your entire employment, sir, with the MUP, what has been the course, custom, and practice with respect to stamps and seals used by organs of the MUP? Have they been registered with a central body in the headquarters of the MUP?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: All stamps would come directly from the MUP, and then they would go through the centre of the public security, and they would come to the police station or the public secure station. The old stamps would be destroyed. A record of that would be made. A new stamp would be made. There would be a commission to certify that such and such stamps were destroyed. This report would be returned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you say that was the practice in 1992?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I cannot guarantee about 1992 because the situation was chaotic at that time, but -- yeah, I cannot guarantee for that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And for the stake of clarity, the gentleman whose signature is listed on this document, Risto Perisic, are you familiar with that individual and the position that he held within the MUP in 1992 in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That was the chief of the Visegrad public security station in that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I think we're done with that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe you mentioned two more documents that you had found in the safe in the commander's office upon assuming that function.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we can have P214 up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I'd ask you if you recognise, is this the list from June of 1992 that you had mentioned? The unsigned --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have the whole page up on the screen. Yeah, there we go.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I believe that -- and the bottom is unsigned. Is this the one you mentioned, the unsigned list from June of 1992 that you found in your safe?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, that is not the list. The list -- this is a salary list. What I found was just a list of names of members of the police force from June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And just for the record, we earlier talked about a Dragan Tomic. If we can look at the entry at line 7 on this document, this Prosecution Exhibit, it indicates Dragan Tomic, "kommandir stanice." Does that comport with your recollection of the Dragan Tomic you talked about earlier who was not on that master list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Tomic Dragan is on this list, and that is the Tomic Dragan, the commander of the police station, just as it says on the list. I think that this list is authentic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Trying to locate the document that you mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If we could have document P210 on the list. I apologise. I'm not sure if that's the ... It's a different document. Is that Exhibit P210?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, do you recall if the other document that you had found in your safe, whether it was handwritten or typed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Typed on a typewriter.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: So is this one of the documents that you found in the safe when you inherited the office?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, no. It was just a classic list of members, and it didn't say police, but "militia," "militia," on the list, and there were no numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you've already clarified for us the extent of the documents that you discovered upon -- upon becoming the commander of the police station in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Sir, at this time, I have no further questions for you. I thank you for your time and your assistance in this matter clarifying some documents. Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber. I'm sorry. I'm sorry for overlooking you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honour. With your leave, I just have a few questions for the questions for this witness, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, you are perfectly entitled, Mr. Cepic. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And I apologise, I didn't mean to jump up.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Uscumlic, I'm Djuro Cepic. I'm the lawyer of -- or attorney for Mr. Sredoje Lukic, and I only have a few questions for you. The first question is, am I correct if I were to say that in view of your important police work experience and the fact that during the war you were also carrying out police duties, am I correct if I say that a policeman cannot be a member of the army at the same time?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, as long as he is a police officer, he cannot be a member of the army also.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens Exhibit 2D60, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, his answer was as long as he is a police officer, he cannot be a member of the army also. But the question that was put in English was, is it correct to say that a policeman cannot be a member of the army. Is there any distinction between a policeman and a police officer?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In our country, it is the same meaning, but I will clarify with a question, Your Honour, with your leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, because of the English translation, perhaps there can be some things that are unclear. I would just like to clarify something. A police officer or just a regular policeman in the war, could either of them be members of the army in any sense?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, they cannot be a member of the army. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I hope that I clarified --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Sir, this document in front of us, did I understand you correctly that you confirmed the authenticity of this document; it's an authentic document that was created in the course of the work of the police station and which you found in the safe?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is the document that I did find in the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have the last page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you agree with me that this stamp at the bottom as well as the name and the signature and the title are authentic and belong to the former chief, Dragan Nisic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have P209, please. Could we leave in that form, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina Ministry of the Interior public security station Trebinje, you would agree with me that that was the form at that time and that place and that that document ought to be authentic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, this is the list that I talked about earlier which I found in the police station. That is that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Uscumlic. [In English] I have just 30 seconds to consult with my client, please. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Uscumlic, one last question for you. At the time the name of the Serbian entity within Bosnia-Herzegovina was Srpska Republika Bosnia and Herzegovina, and later it was changed to Republika Srpska; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] thank you very much. I have no further questions for you, thank you very much. [In English] Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, we will take the break now, so when we resume you can begin your cross-examination. We are adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. My name is Adam Weber from the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'll be asking you some questions here today. I'd like to start out by asking you just a couple of particular questions about your career as a police officer. I'm not going to spend too much time on this as you've already provided many of these answers. Understand? Sir, you began your career with the Gorazde SJB in March of 1987; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, 16 March 1987 in the Security Services Centre of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You were promoted to the commander of the Gorazde SJB in January of 1990; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't know the exact date, but you are probably right.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that a correct approximate date in 1990?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In June of 1992, you were still the commander of the Gorazde SJB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: June 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir, in June of 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No. By that time, I was already a member of the MUP of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the court officer please call up F120-2092 for the witness. I apologise, that's FI20-2092.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the list of active police employees at the Gorazde SJB in June of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you recognise this document as an official document; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document is similar to the documents which you were previously shown from the Visegrad SJB on direct examination?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: In June of 1992, there were approximately -- according to this, there were 33 active members of the Gorazde SJB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your name appears on this list as number 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It indicates that you were the commander of the SJB in Gorazde; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It says commander of the police station. It reads commander of the public security station, but in fact it should be commander of the police station, PS. It's probably a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution would tender this as an Exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P315, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you remained the commander of the Gorazde SJB until May of 1995 when you were promoted to then the position of chief; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you remained the chief of the Gorazde SJB until February of 2003 when that position was abolished, and then you were re-assigned as a commander; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct. I don't know the exact dates, but that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I've had the occasion to speak with Mr. Ivetic during the break. I believe that we can expedite this. The Prosecution at this time would tender into evidence 0645-8089.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That being the decision to appoint this general into the post that he testified to, we stipulate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P316, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Based on your 22 years of experience in command positions, you are familiar with the reports that are regularly sent from the SJB level to the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution have 65 ter -- Prosecution 65 ter 28.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document before you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you are familiar based on your command experience with the police during the war with the types of documents that were sent from the SJB to the MUP during 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: For the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is -- this is an official report to the Ministry of the Interior reporting on the military and security situation in the Serbian territory of Visegrad --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I haven't even finished asking the question. If I could ask the question and then --

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's fine. I'll wait --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, although in the practice to which I'm familiar, once counsel gets up, the other one stops. But go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is an official report to the Ministry of the Interior reporting on the military and security situation in the Serbian territory of Visegrad dated 13 July 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the objection I have is that the counsel is testifying as to facts not in evidence; lack of foundation and speculation as to how this can be claimed to be an official report to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I cannot respond based on Mr. Ivetic's statement already. I'm in the course of laying the foundation. It's cross-examination, so I can lead the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: There's nothing improper in this line of questioning. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'll re-ask my question. This is an official report to the Ministry of the Interior reporting on the military and security situation in the Serbian territory of Visegrad dated 13 July 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, the witness I don't think -- if he has personal knowledge, if that's the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I'm asking --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I have already ruled. Please don't rise again for the same point. Now go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you understand my question, or would you like me to repeat it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I can answer the question, although I didn't read the text through, but the text I don't think is as important as the form.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And this form is an official form that was used in 1992 within the Ministry of the Interior; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but the manner of transmission is not regular. The centre of public security Trebinje was passed over here. It's not logical that this should be sent directly to the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention on the top portion on that page on the right-hand side. There is an indication that this document is an official secret strictly confidential document to be -- by courier; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That's how it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution would tender this document into evidence based on the fact that the witness has already stated that this -- the form of this document is consistent with the official form used at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would object so far as his testimony at page 38, line 16 through 18 specifically denotes a problem with this document that the manner of transmission, i.e., the purported recipient and the purported sending party is improper in his opinion and, therefore, is irregular, so he cannot vouch for the authenticity of this document based upon that evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, that goes to the weight, not the admissibility of this document. It's been noted for the record that. He's indicated that this an official form.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P317, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the court officer could please place page 4 of the B/C/S version and page 6 of the translation on the screen. It will be referred to momentarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, out of the 22 years that you have been a police officer, 19 years have been with the police forces in Gorazde; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Part of it in Gorazde, but when Gorazde was divided into a part that belonged to Republika Srpska and a part that fell under the Federation, I spent until 1992, the part that belonged to Gorazde and the rest of it in Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand what you're saying. What I'm asking, though, is prior to 2006 when you took your current post in Visegrad, you did not work at all within the Visegrad municipality; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: There was a period after I left Gorazde in September, maybe even part of October, we were on record as members. Some of policemen from Gorazde were registered as members of the police of Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could you please define exactly when that period was?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Early September, but I can't give you the exact date, and until the exiled municipality of Gorazde was established.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could please inform us of the year.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: 1992. September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You were not in Visegrad in May or June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not work in the Visegrad SJB throughout the entire course of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I'm telling you, I was working there in September.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Prior to September 1992, you did not work in the Visegrad SJB; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not see if Bosnian Muslims were beaten or killed by members of the police and the reserve military conscripts at the Visegrad SJB between March and August 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No. As I said, I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You do not know how many police officers were regularly appearing for work at the Visegrad SJB between March and August 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If we could please call up the exhibit that we just referenced, P317.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, Mr. Ivetic utilised 56 minutes for his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm not going to take that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Actually, for Exhibit P317, if we could please have the bottom of the first page of the exhibit, which is page 2 of the translation. I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the last paragraph on page 1 of the document in front of you. The report states: "After the withdrawal of the Uzice Corps whose units entered and liberate the central area of town, there was a general mobilisation of military conscripts in the municipality area, and work obligation was introduced for everyone capable of working ..." Could we please continue on page 2 of the B/C/S version. "... with the goal of keeping and expanding the liberated area, which was achieved. Parallel with these activities establishing the army of the Serbian Republic of BH, the 1st Light Brigade of the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was formed in the area of the municipality, under the command of ..." And in the translation could we please turn to the top of page 3. "... Captain 1st Class Vinko Pandurevic, an active-duty officer of the JNA Yugoslav People's Army, while all other officers and soldiers in the brigade are reserve military conscripts from the area of the Serbian Municipality of Visegrad." Is that what that report states?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Ivetic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document speaks for itself. The witness has already testified in response to Mr. Weber's questions that he was not present in Visegrad during the time-period of this report and the time-period of the events that are being specified in this report, so in essence we're having Mr. Weber trying to introduce this, which I would call a written statement of Risto Perisic in contravention of the rules of this Tribunal, Your Honour. So I would object to this manner of trying to authenticate this document with an individual who has already said he has no personal knowledge of the facts that are contained therein.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could please respond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document is in evidence, the 65 ter summary said that this witness would come and speak to the events of the police in relation to Milan Lukic and his status as a reservist in the police at the time. This is relevant to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: The document is already in evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Correct, Your Honour. You admitted it as P317.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. You just admitted it without foundation, and that's the -- that was the objection, was lack of foundation because this is a document that he had never seen before, and all he could say was it was irregular on its face, but he said it was irregular because these kind of documents were never transmitted as this document stated. Therefore, it does not appear regular, and it is a statement of Mr. Perisic where they're attempting to get in through improper witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, it's a question of weight, Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is this what the document states? That's all I'm asking you right now. I'm not asking you to opine on it at all.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've mentioned that you recognise Milan Lukic by sight and that you were present in the Visegrad municipality during 1992. Are you aware that there's evidence in this case that Milan Lukic was a commander in this brigade that's referred to as of the 19th of May, 1992? And for the record, it's Exhibit P314 that's being referred to. Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: You mean this brigade, the name of which you've just read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm asking you your personal knowledge, if you are personally aware, aside from this document, of whether or not Milan Lukic was the commander of the brigade that's referenced in this document.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I haven't seen any reference to Milan Lukic in this document. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I am asking, sir, are you aware? Is that a no, you are saying that you don't know if Milan Lukic was commander or not in that brigade?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could we please have page 3 of the B/C/S version of this exhibit, and page 4 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to read you another portion of this document and then ask you questions based off of it. I'm just going to ask you if the document states what it does.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: Your Honour, objection. This witness is not brought as a verification of the translation. I think this is improper questioning of this witness. He either has a question or he doesn't. But to have him read the statement into the record and verify as to translation is improper.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's not what I'm doing, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What are you doing, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can make a proffer. At this portion, the document refers to the number of policemen that were in the Visegrad SJB at the time. I would like to read him that portion and ask him if that's consistent with his understanding of the level of personnel in that unit, then secondly refers to disciplinary problems within that police department.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, I submit to you that he have to have foundation for his knowledge of the personnel in the unit or in the region.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Lay that foundation, and then you can ask questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you were just shown a number of documents relating to the personnel in the Visegrad SJB from June 1990 through -- all the way through 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: You mean these earlier documents, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes. And you were able to look at those documents, and you answered the questions of both Mr. Ivetic and Mr. Cepic relating to the personnel that was were in the Visegrad SJB between, actually, 1991 and 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document states: "Pursuant to the directives, the reserve police forces of the police station which numbered 150 policemen when the station began operating were reduced to 40 policemen, taking the criteria which were provided in selecting personnel for work in the police into consideration. However, significant deficiencies and difficulties continue to be present in the consistent performance of duties from their jurisdiction. Apart from general shortcomings, which are a reflection of the war ..." then it lists: "The shortcomings are evident as well as we think and suggest should be resolved by exchanging personnel, that is to say transferring them to work in other public security stations." Sir, you were asked some questions by the Defence attorney of Mr. Sredoje Lukic. You said that once people are in the police, they are not part of the military. Isn't it in fact true that people moved from the police to different police stations during the course of war, and, also, at times people from the police department worked with the militia during the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd only ask for clarification.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Let's do one question at a time. Is it true that people moved from the police to different police stations during the course of war? What is your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not that I know of, at least not during the state of war. I don't know that policemen moved to other police stations, unless perhaps it was a disciplinary measure or a minister or a chief of some police station made a decision to move one person to a different police station.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So the state of war had no effect on the movement of police, the different police stations? They remained -- the fact that there was a war made no difference?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. The second question was, is it true that at times people from the police department worked with the militia during the war?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The question is not clear. You said militia. You probably meant the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's correct, sir. The intended question is the army.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: A policeman could not be a member of the army at the same time. He had to finish his work in the police in order to become officially a member of the army, if that's what you mean.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, that was not my question. My question is whether or not in the performance of their security duties, did police officers work with members of the army during the war?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, since you did later come to the Visegrad SJB in 1992, I'd like to ask you about disciplinary problems within that SUP. P317 states that a special problem --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that my learned friends for OTP already filed a motion related to some disciplinary documents, and we filed the response to the documents, and that is still in procedure. So if my colleague Mr. Weber trying to ask questions related to those -- to that procedure, I think that we already has been discussing in the filing form. Secondly, this witness is -- was not the disciplinary judge, and he could not provide us that material or informations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, we don't know yet, Mr. Cepic, whether the witness is able to provide information. What is this about a motion having been filed? Are you saying that the question that has been asked relates to a motion that has been filed and which has not yet been disposed of?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I found a list of exhibits for potential use with this witness from OTP, and they put on that list documents for disciplinary record of my client. And if Prosecutor is trying to ask any question related to that file, I would like just to remind that they filed a couple of days ago motion -- bar table motion with a request for admission of those documents. We responded on Monday related to that material, to that OTP motion, and it is still pending.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic is correct. There is a pending bar table motion. However, Mr. Cepic's objection is one that goes to the authenticity of the documents. We have a witness here who could potentially authenticate them live, present in court. Prosecution would like to make use of that time to authenticate the documents with the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would like to remind my learned friend to read carefully our response, and we added something which is not disclosed to us. We added some -- but we filed everything. I don't want to spend this time to discuss about something which we already filed, Your Honour. Everything is in hard copy. Everything is on the paper.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but what is to prevent the Chamber dealing with it now? Do you know in the jurisdiction from which I come, we don't have this business of filing motions. You get up in court, and you make your submission, and the Judge rules on it. Personally speaking, I find the filing of motions to be quite time-wasting. Too many motions are filed. So let us hear what is your objection, and let us see whether we can deal with it now, and we hear from Mr. Weber. What is your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: This witness cannot -- I'm sorry, is it my turn, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you. This witness cannot provide us any relevant information about disciplinary procedures. That is my point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I haven't been afforded the opportunity to ask this witness what his knowledge is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: No, no. Sorry, I didn't hear your reply.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution hasn't had the opportunity yet to ask this witness what his knowledge would be to authenticate the records. We haven't gotten to that stuff yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Well, go ahead, and if you are getting to that step, make sure that you lay a foundation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, it is important to have discipline amongst the officers who are under your command. You would agree with that; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You would not consider an officer who steals property or refuses orders of his superiors to be a good or reputable officer, would you?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I think that these questions are leading us in completely different way. I will clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Sit. I agree with you, Mr. Cepic. You haven't established any basis for this witness to provide that kind of evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If I may proceed, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As a commander, you are familiar with the disciplinary procedures and records for police officers within the SJB; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, he has to specify which SJB. There are several.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What is the SJB?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Within the -- well, sir, you've testified in multiple different levels within the Ministry of Interior; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And at the lowest level is the police station; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And when I refer to SJB, do you understand that to mean that I'm referring to the lower levels of the Ministry of Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: At that time, these were not the lowest levels, the public security stations, but now they have been abolished, so now they were only -- there are only four public security stations in the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you're familiar with the disciplinary records and procedures from 1992 onwards that were of use in the security stations with the MUP; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the court officer please call up ERN 0645-2835 through 0645-2836.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you recognise this as an official request to institute disciplinary proceedings dated 20 August 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. More or less, that's what it looks like in the request.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, you recognise the form of this document as the official form used in relation to the disciplinary proceedings; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The subject of this request is Sredoje Lukic; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the item numbers in this request, which are in the middle of the page of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
