utterances.text: I have to object. This witness clearly said that he came in September 1992 in police station of Visegrad, so he cannot provide us any relevant information for previous period. Secondly, I must underline that in the record. From OTP, we have obstruction in relation to disclosure material several times. We requested many times, and we filed that in a motion, to provide us with all material. We didn't receive clear answers, and we clearly -- our position is clear in relation to this request. If they got decision from disciplinary procedure, we would be very grateful to see that decision on the screens. The request doesn't mean anything without decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, this is just a -- Your Honours, this is the first -- [French on English channel]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, start again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. Your Honour, this is the first in a sequence of documents. I believe Mr. Cepic has the opportunity to submit additional documents that he might feel are relevant in relation to this matter. He has requested alternative relief in that circumstance, and his response, I would note for the Chamber, that this witness -- the 65 ter summary says the witness is the current commander of the Visegrad police. He will testify as to the official documentation from the Visegrad police station and the manner of record-keeping. This witness will testify as to the manner of operation and functioning of the SJB Visegrad. He has clearly been brought here and Mr. Cepic has been put on notice in relation to this individual's testimony. We are asking him about documents which he has clearly indicated he is familiar with.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic says that he only arrived at the police station in September 1992, and this document relates to August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Cepic has noted, this is the first in a sequence of documents. The later ones will carry over there. However, the Prosecution would note that that is in the context of this witness already saying that he is familiar with this document, that's it's in the official form, that he recognizes it, that he's got over 20 years of experience in being familiar with the disciplinary procedures of the Security Services Centre. So I believe this witness has sufficient ability to authenticate the document and actually as of now already has authenticated the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, with your leave, this witness cannot provide us any relevant information from this document and from other documents which Prosecutor intend to show us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Why not if he has familiarity with the kind of document that this one is?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Prosecutor did not try to establish that is this witness familiar with this informations and with -- this simply not a record of Sredoje Lukic. I think that he firstly has to establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Prosecution would tender this exhibit at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, we admit it.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P318, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would like to note that there is actually two versions that we prepared in relation to the document since it does have a sensitive name, and we'd ask that the unredacted version be admitted under seal and the redacted version be also admitted. I apologise for not mentioning that upfront. If we could please not have this broadcast to the public too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: In this case, Your Honours, Exhibit P318 is under seal, and the redacted version is Exhibit P319.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in this document item number 1 indicates that Mr. Sredoje Lukic appropriated a motor vehicle --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute. Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could Prosecutor establish any knowledge of this witness related to any information related to Sredoje Lukic from disciplinary procedure against him?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I've already admitted the document, Mr. Cepic. You may raise that in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this document indicates that Sredoje Lukic misappropriated a motor vehicle under item 1, exceeded his official powers under item number 3, and refused to obey legal orders of the chief and commander of the Visegrad SJB under item number 5. My question to you is based on your --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Where is item number 5?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. That's on page 2 of the translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: All right. Can we see page 2. Yes. Proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, in your significant experience as a commander in the security services, you would not consider an officer who steals property or refuses orders of the superiors to be a good or reputable officer, would you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: First of all, I would like to say that this is the first time that I'm seeing this document, so I can speak generally about policemen, but I cannot say anything about this specific matter. If you are asking me if a policeman were to do something as it is stated here, probably I would also initiate disciplinary proceedings against such a policeman. But as I said, I'm seeing this document for the first time. I have never seen it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you had such a disciplinary problem with one of your officers, would you seek to terminate their employment?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I can just submit a request to initiate proceedings, but the disciplinary commission which was working then, now it's a matter that goes before the disciplinary court, so then the disciplinary commission would decide about the fate of the policeman. They would investigate, gather evidence, and decide what the outcome would be for that particular policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you would seek to do that if you had an officer who was stealing property and refusing to obey orders; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Of course, a manager officer is obliged to investigate, to see what happened, and if he should gather evidence on the matter, then he would be duty-bound to initiate proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the court officer please call up ERN 0645-2837. 0645-2837. I apologise, it's actually part of the previous exhibit. If we could go back to Exhibit P318. I believe it's the last exhibit, the last page, which is ERN 0645-2837.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is a dispatch from the chief of the MUP dated 7 October 1992 with a sequential dispatch number. You recognise this official form; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the last sentence of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think this witness could not provide us any reliable information related to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, you haven't established any familiarity on the part of the witness with a document of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, Your Honour, I'm just looking at the document for the first time on the screen. Do they have one with an official stamp on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Judge, I am in the course of doing these things, laying the foundations, If I could be allowed to examine based on the document. When I go to tender, the Prosecution would be happy to respond to whatever the foundational objections are by both counsel.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but you need to lay the foundation before you ask him to comment on the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you've already indicated that this is the official format used for dispatches with the MUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you recognise the dispatch number on this document as being part of the regularly used sequential numbering used in dispatches in 1992; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, the numbers would change, so I cannot remember exactly which the numbers -- which numbers were used in that period. The organisational units would often change these numbers, so I'm not quite sure. I cannot really tell you precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. I understand it's going back a long time. I am not asking you to recall the exact numbering of the document, but this is consistent with the numbering that was used in 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. It's just this first number 09-30 is too low. I think there should be another digit there, in my opinion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, you recognise this format as being from the CSB Trebinje; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The format is all right. The signature is all right. I'm just saying that this number is not logical. It's not quite right that there is 09 and then the number immediately. There should be another number indicating the organisational unit that would go in between these two numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I understand, sir. You recognise this signature as the signature of the chief of the centre, Krsto Savic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I cannot really talk specifically about the signature, but the chief at the time was Krsto Savic. I cannot attest as to the signature, however.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This document is consistent with the regular dispatches that you would receive at that time as a member of the security services?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: More or less, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to direct your attention to the last line, but before even getting to that, this document involves Sredoje Lukic again; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The last sentence of this dispatch states: "The measure of termination of employment has been --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is calling for speculation. This witness as is confirmed in this transcript could not provide us any reliable information about disciplinary procedure against Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And I don't think he is doing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm just authenticating the document and verifying what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And this is beyond of direct examination. We already have admitted request. I prepared decision here with me, and we will have the full picture. We will have the full -- all informations related to this procedure. I'm so glad to request admission of procedure -- that procedure, and it is in my hands right now in hard copy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: But that doesn't prevent the Prosecutor from examining on this document. I don't see anything improper in this line of questioning, Mr. Cepic. Continue, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this dispatch states in the last sentence: "The measure of termination of employment has been pronounced against the named party." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And you said that you were in Visegrad in September and October 1992. This document I see is dated the 7th of October, 1992. Are you aware -- did you know Sredoje Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: When I arrived, Sredoje Lukic was not working at the Visegrad police station anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was it your understanding at that time that he had already been terminated?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Nobody said anything. In any case, he was not working. He wasn't at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, are you aware of any police officers that murdered or raped any Bosnian Muslim civilians in Visegrad in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You identified a bunch of payroll lists during your direct examination. I'd like to ask you about one name in particular. On all those payroll lists was a Mr. Boban Simsic. Do you know that person?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you aware that Boban Simsic was convicted for crimes against humanity by the court in Bosnia-Herzegovina on the 7th August, 2007, under case number XKRZ0504 for murder and rape of Bosnian civilians in June of 1992? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And despite your previous answer, you are aware that Boban Simsic, then, was a reserve police officer in the Visegrad SUP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: This appears to be beyond the scope of direct examination, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We have been through that kind of objection before, and the rules permit the cross-examiner to put his case.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And when the only other issue, then, would be the relevance, Your Honour, due to the fact that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Okay. What is the relevance, Mr. Weber?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, he said that he wasn't aware of any police officers from the Visegrad SJB committing murder or rape of a Bosnian civilian, and then two questions later he has now said that he is aware of one of those police officers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Credibility. All right. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, you said that you responded to requests for assistance by both parties in this case; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Could you please repeat your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You have responded in your official capacity to requests that have been made by the parties in this case; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, and the other procedures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've received requests from both the Defence and the Prosecution in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You've been listed as a witness for the accused Milan Lukic since 19 November 2008. When were you first contacted to be a witness in this case by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I did not know that I would be a witness for the Defence until I came here; then people from the Tribunal told me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Have you ever met with anyone from the Defence prior to you coming to The Hague?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, with Mr. Ivetic when he came to submit that request for us to run those checks. He came officially to the police station and submitted that request.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So with respect to that request, Mr. Ivetic actually delivered that to you in person?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did he inform you at that time -- I'm sorry, sir. If there's something that you want to add, please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. He filed it with the protocol section.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did he tell you that when he arrived?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He came and brought the request, and then I told him to go to the protocol section to have it filed so that it is assigned a certain number.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was it explained to you at all at that time that you may be a witness in this case?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't remember hearing that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was this the first time you met Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, the first and the last.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: How long did you meet with Mr. Ivetic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Fifteen minutes or so, but let me correct myself regarding this mention of myself as a possible witness. It was mentioned, and that's when I said that it would be a better idea for some of the professionals involved in that kind of work to be invited as a witness, somebody who is directly involved in that sort of work.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, just five minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This occurred between the 27th and 30th of January; correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to please call up -- actually, recall 1D22-0800 and the corresponding 1D22-0802.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to direct your attention to the sentence immediately above where it states "annex A." Do you see that portion?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It states: "We are conveying for individuals we have located in our evidence, under number 12 of the above-mentioned letter ." That's what the response that you provided states; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: These are sequential numbers taken from your letter, from your request. This might be a typo.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I am not asking you about the numbers that are listed beneath annex A. I'm asking you particularly about the sentence that appears above where it says "annex A." It says that you are conveying for individuals we have located in our evidence under number 12 of the above-mentioned letter. That's what that states; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, he just read the sentence back and made the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, is that what that sentence says?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That's what it says, but it's a typo. The typist when they typed this made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, in terms of --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, I'd like to show you, then, 1D22-0814. The corresponding B/C/S version is 1D22-0815.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see this document in front of you? Actually, I believe we just have the English version.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Does he have the corresponding B/C/S version in front of you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can assist, it's 1D22-0815 it's the B/C/S. It's part of the same -- it's the second page of the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Second page of the same exhibit, it should be. It's one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, can you see the document in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: There is no item number 12 in that letter; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, misstates the evidence. He has made the correction as to what the typographical error was, and they can direct him to what he relied upon. I mean, they're trying to make a mountain out of a molehill here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just answer the question, and let's move on.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is there no item 12 in this request?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: There's no -- it makes no sense that it should be 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. Is that a "yes," then; there's no item 12?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's right. There's no sense in 12. It's just a typo. You can look at the same document sent to the MUP of Republika Srpska. In their copy, there is no such mistake, I suppose.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Your response to this request was on the 30th of January, 2009. You conducted your entire investigation within three days; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Once I delivered the list to the civil servant engaged in that work, he ran the checks the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is that all you did?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: After I received the list, I submitted it to the civil servant in charge because it a certain procedure. The document was filed, registered. When it reached my desk, I sent it to CIPC. I gave it to the civil servant, who manually looked up the files, ran the checks, and gave me back -- came up that list.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. You did not go to Koritnik or any of the residences in Visegrad that you found the addresses of to verify if these individuals were still alive, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, no. All the work was only done based on the files because we had no more details, just name, surname, and approximate age.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you did not check any census data to verify if these individuals were alive back in 1991 as part of this request, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, no, just the files.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't check any of the current voting records to verify if any of these individuals were still currently alive as part of this request, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object, beyond the scope, and it's beyond the scope of the document itself because the request is right before us. We've been sitting there looking at it for the last ten minutes. It clearly states what was asked and what was responded to. His response has nothing do with whether or not people are alive or dead, and he has not testified as to that, so the questions by Mr. Weber are misstating this gentleman's evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: And we can see how good Ms. Tabeau's table ended up being at the final end, so I don't think it's really relevant to put those questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you didn't check any of the current voting records to see if these people were still alive, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: We had no access to those records, and we didn't check them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You didn't place a simply call to the Commission For Missing Persons in Sarajevo to see if there's any information relating to these individuals, did you?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We know -- and that's an improper question. We know how inaccurate that is as well. Lack of foundation for this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Alarid, the objection is not meritorious. Please proceed. You should be coming to an end now, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: These were my last questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You did not even place a call to the Commission For Missing Persons in Sarajevo to see if there were any -- if there was any information relating to these individuals, did you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I had to identify these persons first. How would I ask them for information about certain people if in a database there are dozens of people with the same name and surname?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I just forgot to tender one document. That would be the only thing. It was the last record that was called up for Sredoje Lukic, is the dispatch. It was ERN 0645-2837.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: We object, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: What document is that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That was the dispatch from the chief of the MUP dated 7 October 1992, which he authenticated and laid a foundation for that indicated Mr. Lukic -- Sredoje Lukic was terminated from the employment of the MUP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. You object to it being admitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, because this witness clearly said that there are missing numbers and he couldn't recognise signature on that document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We admit it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I understand it's already been admitted as part of 318.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it then acceptable with the Court to keep it as part of the same exhibit?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Any -- Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. But before I start with my examination, I kindly ask Madam Usher to deliver hard copies of one document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Just a minute, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic, in what capacity are you seeking to ask questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, my client is mentioned several times, and Prosecutor requested admission of some documents related to disciplinary record of my clients. That's the capacity for re-examination. And it is not something which I raised in my examination. This is completely new topic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Re-examination is for Mr. Ivetic. Whose witness this? Who called this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ALARID
utterances.text: We would stipulate to give some of our time to Mr. Cepic, Your Honour. We only have three questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And with your leave, Your Honour, if I may remind, page 53, line 18 and 19.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Counsel is not speaking into the microphone. Nobody can hear him.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... raise in my examination. Oh, I'm sorry. I'm sorry. The reference is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, I had said you could re-examine, although he was not your witness. But you have questions to ask, so ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I could facilitate for counsel. The Prosecution has seen this document before as part of the bar table motion. It's been raised. I believe that Mr. Cepic's request in that regard is fair. We do not oppose admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes. Does that help you?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: It's help me, Your Honour, but I would like to ask just two questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Uscumlic, it's me again. You will agree with me that this document before you is a decision by the Ministry of the Interior?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The public security centre in Trebinje, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Right. Will you look at page 2. The Prosecutor asked you more than once to read certain portions, and I will ask you the same thing. Second page in English and second paragraph in B/C/S, second page, first paragraph. Could you please read the first paragraph on the second page.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: "Violations stated in items 1 and 2 of the request cannot be held against the accused because from the additionally adduced evidence, it cannot be established that the perpetrator of the act in question that he is charged with pursuant to" --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask for admission of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, will you agree with me that in that period that is autumn 1992 -- [In English] I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit 2D65.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Cepic. The witness did not conclude the reading of that sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And maybe it's the important part that's missing.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm sorry. I did not let you finish reading that portion. Will you finish the sentence?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: "... the acts in question that pursuant to Article 286" -- sorry. "... 296 of the Law on State Administration he is charged with."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Cannot be established that the perpetrator of the act in question, that he is charged with pursuant to -- what is the effect of this, Mr. Cepic?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Completely, directly. He is not accused for -- he is not -- in this decision. [Interpretation] In this decision, he is found guilty only for counts 3, 4, 5, not 1 and 2. And in the interests of justice, I should tender this entire document because it provides a broad picture of the entire procedure, and we will later in our arguments present further evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: We will admit it.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, will you agree with me that in the period August, September, October 1992, it was extremely dangerous to travel between Visegrad and Trebinje?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. The roads were cut off, and to reach Trebinje you had to travel via Serbia and Montenegro.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Uscumlic. No further questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, as I indicated, I have three questions. I'll be brief.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Mr. Uscumlic, first of all, the Commission For Missing Persons in Sarajevo, do they have any role in issuing and registering the JMBG registration numbers for persons born in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I apologise for not knowing the name of the agency or the department, but the entity involved in holding voter registration records for Bosnia-Herzegovina, do they have a role in issuing and registering the JMBG numbers for persons born in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And what entity or entities are tasked with keeping the records of persons born in Visegrad and as to the JMBG registration in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Formally, it was the Ministry of the Interior, that is, police stations, and now it is within the jurisdiction of Registrars' offices.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just waiting for the translation. Thank you, sir, and again, I thank you for coming here pursuant to subpoena issued and served upon you. I thank you for assisting us in this matter as a subpoena witness. Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Witness, that concludes your evidence. We thank you for coming to the Tribunal to give it. You may now leave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The next witness in proofing had requested protective measures. I don't know whether Your Honour has been made privy to the e-mail that I circulated as soon as I found that information. If possible, we can go in private and have the witness come in and make the statements herself to Your Honours. She is perhaps in the best position to explain the circumstances of the request for protective measures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, and I'll ask one or two questions, and you will also assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I will try, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, let the witness be brought.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Madam, first of all, can I ask you if you can confirm for me that you came to testify here pursuant to an official subpoena served upon you by the legal organs of the country in which you reside issued by order of this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I was given a summons which I could not refuse, and that is why I am here.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, ma'am, for the record, we -- for the record now, we need to have your full name.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Stoja Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And, madam, could you tell us with respect to your current occupation what you currently do and who you are employed by?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I work at the MUP of Republika Srpska, more specifically in the Visegrad police station where I issue personal ID cards, unique citizens identity numbers, and the CIPS system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I'll wait for the translation and the transcript to catch up with us. You've mentioned the that this is part of the CIPS system within the structure of the MUP. Could you describe for us or explain what the CIPS, C-I-P-S, system is?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. These are civilian affairs that are under the jurisdiction of the MUP, the issuance of personal ID cards, and it's like working in an agency that is actually part of the MUP. We are actually paid by the MUP. We are part of the MUP structure. Our bosses are within the MUP structure.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And I presume you had to report to the MUP and obtain their acquiescence to you coming here pursuant to the subpoena rather than as a willing witness; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How long have you so been employed in this particular department within the umberance [sic] -- or within the penumbra of the MUP of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I have been in the MUP since 1986, but the CIPS agency began to work on the 27th of October, 2003.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: You mentioned that one of the tasks with which your current position is empowered relates to JMBG or JMBG numbers, the unique identifier numbers, I guess, is how it came up in the transcript. If I can ask you, please, what is your understanding of the current law and regulation as to whether or not the registration of an individual born and/or living in Bosnia-Herzegovina requires a JMBG, and how long has that law been in effect?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: The law has been in force since 1980. In 1980, they began to issue unique personal identification numbers for citizens, and it's part of the Law on Administrative Affairs of Republika Srpska, the then Bosnia-Herzegovina, and so on. This was in effect on the territory of the whole of Yugoslavia, this law of 1980, and it exists to this day. This is an identification number. If you know a person's unique identification number, then you can have all data about them, who they are, where they were born, where their place of residence is, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And at what time is the JMBG issued or given to an individual who is a citizen of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Immediately on birth. Persons who were born before 1980 and did not have a JMBG were given one retroactively. Parties would come and receive this number, or the number was issued on the basis of personal identification file cards, but for those who were born after 1980 they received -- or newborns would receive this number immediately.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the registration system, is it possible for more than one -- for more than one individual to have the same JMBG number?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's possible, but it can only be the result of an error. Once we started automatic data processing or computer data processing, you could not have one JMBG for two persons. This is impossible. Computer would not accept such data.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I've gotten a little bit ahead of myself. I want to take things chronologically. If I could try to direct your attention back to the year 1992, and I believe you had indicated that you had been working in the MUP since sometime in the '80s. I believe you said 1986. If you could please tell us, in 1992 what position of employment or duties did you have within the MUP, specifically in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Personal ID cards issuing certificates about the places of residence or changes of place of residence and the JMBG number.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now focusing on 1992, was there a period of time when you had occasion when you had to leave Visegrad for any reason whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Okay. And I want to focus on -- first of all, did you return to Visegrad; and if so, what month did you return to work in the Visegrad police station in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: On the 27th of March, 1992, we had to leave the SUP. All the Serb employees had to leave, and I returned to work -- actually, I returned from Serbia on the 15th of June, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And when you returned from Serbia in June, the second half of June 1992 and when you returned to the police station to work, during that time-period in June 1992, did you have an occasion to see Milan Lukic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Where did you have occasion to see him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: At the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: How was Mr. Milan Lukic dressed on those occasions when you saw him at the police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Blue camouflage uniforms worn by the police at that time, and they also had yellow green camouflage uniforms as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: What can you tell us about your knowledge as to Milan Lukic in June of 1992? What organisation or security force was he a member of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I don't know, and I don't have any information about him being in some other organisation. I would see him at the police station. When I would come to work, I would go to my office. I would sometimes meet some colleagues; sometimes I wouldn't. But in any case, for the most part I would see him when I was at work.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, ma'am, now we can return to your time-period of the present day. Did you have -- in the course of your duties working in the department for ID cards and ID numbers and change of address, did you have occasion to be tasked by your commanding officer with responding to a request for assistance from the Defence in this case, for myself, relating to the JMBG dates of birth and father's last name as to a certain list of individuals?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. My commander brought me a list recently and told me to find everything in the old database, the file cards with those first and last names, which is what I did because this is my job. It's part of my job description.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: If I can ask you first of all, you said to look everything in the old database. Where is the old database housed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: In my office, actually. It's in a corridor where I work. It's part of the CIPS system.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And that database, the old database, if you could tell us what kinds of records make a part of it, what it consists of?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: These are just file cards for personal identification cards before the electronic data processing. Before 2003 when personal ID cards were issued, the original of the card would be given to the party. There would be just one original. There would not be a copy of it. But there were some file cards which would have a fingerprint, a photograph and signature of the party, and all of their personal data, their first and last name, name of parents, when they were born, where, and the place of residence. On the back of the card, there would be changes in place of residence noted. If somebody, for example, moved from Visegrad to Gorazde, you would note down the time when they stopped being a resident of Visegrad and became a resident of Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And on this -- and on this occasion when you were tasked by your commander to perform this search, did you have occasion to see the actual letter from me and the list enclosed therein as to the individuals that were to be searched for?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I had the list because I had to look for the file cards according to the list.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you able to find all the individuals from that list based upon the information given within the bounds of your manual search through the physical records, the physical database?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: This is not so difficult to do the search because if you have one last name, you will take that last name and you will take out all the persons with that last name that is on the list. It's in alphabetical order, anyway, so this is something that is very easy to find.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And once you performed this task and obtained the information in the physical cards of the individuals from the list, did you take any part in drafting the response by the police station in Visegrad and your commander Zoran Uscumlic to the Defence relating to this information that was found, or did you just report it to him?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It was my job to find all of those file cards and to hand over the file cards to him with a record of how many file cards I handed over. As for the reply, I mean, we had to note down if somebody changed their last name or their place of residence. We would check back on the file card. We would enter the JMBG into the CIPS system, and then with that number, it would immediately show up where that person was currently residing if it was registered in the CIPS. So I noted all of those changes, and then I handed over all those file cards and records to my commander, and then, actually, I didn't have anything more to do with actually replying to this particular request.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the CIPS system, am I correct that -- well, let me give you -- let me see how it came out in the transcript. You are recorded in the transcript as saying: "We would enter the JMBG into the CIPS system and with that number it would immediately show up where that person is currently residing ..." Is that true for persons that would be residing outside of Bosnia-Herzegovina, or is it limited to those living within Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes. No, no. Only in Bosnia so we could check where somebody was living if we had their JMBG number. Outside of the borders of Bosnia and Herzegovina, we are not able to do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And were you able to -- given the list that you were given, were you able to find for every person on that list a file card correlating to the name, last name, and the approximate age that was listed on the list from the indictment that was presented to you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, let me remember an example. I know there was a family name of Kurspahic. I was actually born there, so I'm familiar with it. It was written Aisa Kurspahic, born approximately 1940. So of all the -- all the Aisas born in approximately 1940 we singled out. The JMBG number was missing. There was no father's name or mother's name, and we can't know precisely which Aisa it was. We could have narrowed it down with the name of the father or some other detail. So we had to make a list of all the Aisa Kurspahics born around 1940 that we came up with.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I have to wait for the English to catch up with us even though I sometimes have a tendency to want to ask you a follow-up question before the translation is finished. With respect to the list that you were given, were there individuals for whom you could not find a corresponding file card that matched the name and the approximate age that was listed on the list?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. For instance, there were some children listed as around 1, 2, or 3, and they could not even have had card files. They would have to be at least 18 when one becomes eligible for an ID. Formally, children were entitled to be issued with an ID card below 18 with the consent of the parents. However, very few children availed themselves of that possibility. They simply don't have ID cards.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you've sufficiently described the process behind the response to the request from the Defence in your present-day role with respect to the dates of birth and JMBG numbers. To get back to the time-period of 1992 and the wartime period in Visegrad, for the sake of clarity, do you recall, who was the commander of the police station in 1992 in June when you returned?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: In June, it was Dragan Tomic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And do you recall what happened to Mr. Tomic?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. He got killed.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Do you recall when it was that he was killed?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I remember one of his -- one of our colleagues got killed on the 19th of June, and on the 20th -- 21st, rather, three of our colleagues got killed, among them, Mr. Tomic, Mr. Andric, and another one.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, madam. I have no further questions for direct examination. Again, I thank you for coming here in response to our subpoena to assist us in this manner. Your Honours, I pass the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: With your leave, very briefly, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, ma'am. I'm Djuro Cepic, Defence counsel for Sredoje Lukic. I have few questions for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] and I would like to call up 2D00-1663.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, can I get my glasses?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you see the screen?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, but can we enlarge this, the right-hand list.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask the upper part of document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That's a list of employees, payroll.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you go down to number 22.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: On the right-hand side. That's me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Stoja Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Look at 13, please. It says Sredoje Lukic. Can you please read what is written there next to his name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic, secondary education, suspended on the 19th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Would you like to authenticate the document?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we have the second page, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Is this an authentic document issued at your station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I would kindly ask admission of this document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D66, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Ma'am, we can see here that Sredoje Lukic was suspended from duty on the 19th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I hear you and the interpreter at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Sorry. On the first document shown to you, we saw that Sredoje Lukic was suspended on the 19th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Until that day, did he perform all his duties as a regular active duty policeman at the police station in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Could we have on our screens 2D00-1665, please. And could we zoom in number 22, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would you please look at 22.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: In the right-hand corner, do you see your signature?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you scroll up.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Do you see what this document refers to?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's the payroll for September 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at 14.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic. I can see it's Lukic Sredoje, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Will you please listen to my questions. In this table, we see minus 30 percent next to Sredoje Lukic's name, and we see that it's payment for the month of September. Did he get a deduction of 30 percent because he was suspended?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Of course. If you are suspended, then your salary is reduced.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: I kindly ask admission of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Thank you. Exhibit 2D67.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And the last document is 2D00-1668.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, in regard to this document I have only one question. We see that it's a list of personnel for the purposes of payment of salaries for the month of October 1992. Will you look at number 22, please. Is that your name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. Stoja Vujicic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: And how about number 13?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Sredoje Lukic, and then suspended on the 19th of August, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, ma'am. I have no further questions. May I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 2D68, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, madam. My name is Stevan Cole. I will be asking you some questions on behalf of the Prosecution. Just a little bit about yourself, firstly. What is your maiden name?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Bozic.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you're an Orthodox Serb?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you are age 46?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you were born on - I'll spell it - B-l-a-c-e in the Visegrad municipality?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And this is not very far distant from Klasnik and Rujiste; is that right?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And are you aware or do you believe that Milan Lukic comes from Rujiste?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain he was born in Rujiste. In fact, he lived in Rujiste. I can't remember exactly if he was born there. For instance, I was born somewhere in the countryside. I don't know where he was born exactly, but he grew up in Rujiste.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. Now, have you effectively lived your whole life in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you have effectively worked your whole life in Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. And I went to school there, and I've worked my whole life in Visegrad.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And you've worked in one capacity or another for the police for your whole working career?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, presently are you a civilian police employee, a civilian employed at the police station?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. And I have always worked as a civilian employed by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you've never worked as a police officer, an active or permanent police officer, even though your name appears on the list of permanent police staff?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, you have to understand one thing. We who work in administration, things like issuing IDs, registration for vehicles or driver's licences, et cetera, we were never police officers, but we are in the same police station. We work for the Ministry of the Interior. We are not the same as policemen, but we share the same building.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. I thank you for that explanation. I wonder if you could help us with just short answers if you can. If it needs longer to explain, then, of course, I don't want to cut you short. So the work that you explained before in your answer, for example, the JMBG, is that the sort of work you've been doing for over 20 years?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Did you at one stage work as a traffic officer in June of 1992? Did you go out working with the traffic at some stage?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, never. I never worked as a policeman, a traffic policeman or any other kind of policeman.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If I have time later, I might put a document to you that indicates that on the 23rd of June you had some work as a traffic officer, and you'll be able to explain that at that stage. Now, your home address now, is it the same address that you were living in 1992 when you returned to Visegrad, in June?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No. Until then, I rented an apartment. In fact, I rented an apartment until late last year. I only recently got my apartment -- an apartment that I owned.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: And that was a change of address.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Where were you living when -- in June of 1992? What part of Visegrad?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: It's Vidovdanska Street.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is that in the centre of town, or how far from, let's say, the old bridge is that address?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Perhaps two kilometres, maybe a kilometre and a half. I can't tell you exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And where were you working? Which particular building were you working in in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, that is close to my apartment, too, but on the other side of the bridge. Both the SUP and my apartment were close to the exit from the town.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: If you could just do it shortly for me, if you would, were you working in a police building or a police station in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's the police building, and there was only one police building, one police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And where exactly is that in relation to the river or a bridge? Can you give us some idea? Somewhere near the old bridge or the new bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, it's closer to the old bridge than to the new bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What is the distance from the police station where you were working to the old bridge?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. Perhaps a kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Okay. So did you have to cross either the old bridge or the new bridge when you were going from your home to work in 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, no. Because my apartment was perhaps 300 to 400 metres away from the SUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: It's your evidence that you returned to Visegrad on the 23rd of June, 1992. How can you be sure of that date?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Which statement? This is the first time I'm giving any sort of evidence before anyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Sorry, I have the date wrong. It's the 15th of June. It was your evidence it was the 15th of June, I'm sorry, that you -- your evidence that you returned, I think, from Serbia to Visegrad. So is that date correct or not?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: That is correct. I now testify that that is the correct date of my return because on the 27th of March when we left the SUP, I did not come back to Visegrad until the 15th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So how do you know it was the 15th of June?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Because I know that it's the Holy Trinity, our Serbian holiday, and it falls always on a Sunday, and I know that I returned the first day after the Holy Trinity, and I returned to work.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: And so what day of the week was the 15th of June, 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Monday. Because the Holy Trinity is always on a Sunday. The date can change but not the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: So you were employed by the police department, if we can call it that, from I think you said 1986, and you are still employed by the department today?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: I just want to ask you about the period then when you returned to Visegrad in 1992 say through to the end of the war in Bosnia in 1995. Did you continue to receive your police pay on a regular basis during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Not immediately. I only started to work sometime around the 1st of July, and until I started to work, of course I received no salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: You were paid, weren't you, from -- certainly from June 1992; isn't that correct? You were paid that month?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Could we have Exhibit P209, please, the first page in B/C/S and in English. In fact, it's the second page in English. P209.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Can you see that on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Is that a similar list as was shown to you a short time ago by Mr. Cepic, but this time it's the for the month of June 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: We can see your name there, can't we, at number 20?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Would you concede, then, that you were wrong a short time ago and that in fact you were paid certainly in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, that's not wrong. This is a list of employees, and the payroll kept at the bank is another thing. I know that I did not receive my salary. I had a temporary replacement, a stand-in, and if anyone got the salary at that time, it was her.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. Well, then this time will you have a look, please, at P214.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: The first page in B/C/S, and it's the first going over to the second pages of the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Now, this is the pay record for June 1992, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Do you think maybe you have made a mistake about being paid in June 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: No, I'm certain. Look, it says "Stoja Vujicic - Jela," and the person who collected the salary at the bank was Jela, Jela Rosic who occupied my place until I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I wonder -- Your Honour, it's been brought to my attention that exhibits that are being shown to the witness are in fact confidential, so I wonder if we can take steps so that they aren't broadcast, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: They have not been broadcast.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. So the position is that someone else collected your pay, you're telling us, for June, and was it the following month, July, you once again collected your pay?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: I really can't remember about July, but I'm certain about June, that I did not go there myself and collect it, the salary.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: All right. That can be taken from the screen. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, then, let's just summarise, then. Certainly from about July 1992 through until 1995, did you collect your pay as a police employee on a regular basis during that period?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, if that's what you call regular. I received them because from the 4th of October, 1992, I was on sick leave. Later, in fact, I was on maternity leave, but our law allows for two years of maternity leave for your third child.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Well, then, for the most part you were continuing to receive pay for, let's say, two years from July 1992?

utterances.speaker: ZORAN USCUMLIC
utterances.text: Well, to the extent that they were paid out, I received them because you get 100 percent of your salary while you are in sick leave, no deductions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Cole, as you know, we stop at 10 minutes after 7.00, so I have to ask, how much longer will you be?

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: What I can indicate, Your Honour, is that I will, in light of the examination-in-chief that I've heard, cut down the cross-examination that I have so that I -- certainly within, let's say, half an hour or so, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have to keep it to about 20 minutes. The examination-in-chief was 23 minutes. But we'll have to resume tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. COLE
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: So we'll adjourn until tomorrow at 8.50 a.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
